newsitem.title: USA: Investigators sketchy on Iowa hog disease probe.
newsitem.headline: Investigators sketchy on Iowa hog disease probe.

text.p: Animal health investigators on Monday declined any substantial comment on a stepped-up probe in Iowa into an apparent new strain of hog disease that kills pregnant sows and sometimes baby pigs.

"There have been isolated reports of individual cases in the past year but the situation increased during the past two months," Beth Lautner, a veterinarian for the National Pork Producers Council, told a teleconference from Clive, Iowa.
The new disease is similar to Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome but has a higher mortality rate for sows than seen in the past, Lautner said.
State officials said on Monday that scattered cases of the disease had been reported in southeast Iowa on small to medium-sized farms. Officials declined to say what county or counties were affected.
"Several thousand hogs" have been affected, according to Jack Ratekin of the Iowa Agriculture Department.
Epidemiologists from the U.S. Agriculture Department's Animal Plant Health Inspection Service joined the probe on Monday, Lautner said.
"We asked APHIS to conduct an epidemiology investigation to coordinate efforts with local producers and practitioners," Lautner said.
Iowa is the number one U.S. pork-producing state.

The APHIS field team will be gathering information on the affected herds to try to determine how the disease moves through the herds and on to other herds, said Kevin Petersburg, area veterinarian for APHIS based in Des Moines.
"We're just here to provide the assistance of our epidemiologists to resolve this problem," Petersburg said.
